newsitem.title: USA: James River sees few manufacturing layoffs.
newsitem.headline: James River sees few manufacturing layoffs.

text.p: James River Corp and Fort Howard Corp said the proposed merger of the two companies is expected to have little impact on employment among the companies' manufacturing facilities.

"Most of our people will continue to make the strong products and the strong brands" that are now being manufactured by both companies, said James River chief executive officer Miles Marsh at a press conference to discuss the earlier-announced merger.
However, both companies said some overlap is expected in administrative areas of the company. They were not specific.
Marsh said any antitrust issues surrounding the merger are "manageable"and the companies are hopeful the deal can be concluded without any asset sales.

He also said the transaction is expected to have a significant impact on 1997 earnings, but was not specific. The company previously said it would take an unspecified charge against earnings in connection with the deal.
The deal also includes a break-up fee of $95 million and does not provide any protective pricing mechanism, such as a collar, said James River senior vice president Ernst Haberli.
Marsh declined to describe details of how the merger was formed or which company made the initial approach, only describing the talks as "short, but very intense."
